plan.notes: TRUE degree verified at duq.edu: Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Computer Science, School of Science and Engineering, Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (also offered as B.A.; this plan is the B.S.). Term-by-term sequence transcribed manually from the official 'Sample Course Work' on the program page; course codes, titles, and per-course credits verified against the 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog requirements page. Catalog year used: 2026-2027. Catalog degree minimum is 120 credits; the program page requires 120. CREDIT DISCREPANCY (documented honestly): the sample page prints term totals of 16/16/16/15, 14/15, 16/17, 15, and 12 (summing to 120), but Spring Year 4 lists five 3-credit courses (capstone + 2 COSC electives + 2 general electives = 15), so its printed '(12 credits)' header conflicts with its own course list — almost certainly a typo on the source page. The catalog's per-course credits for the listed courses sum to 123 on the BIOL/PHYS science path (125 with CHEM); total_credits is set to 123 = the sum of encoded course credits so the file stays internally consistent. Science sequence choice: BIOL 111/112 (4+4), CHEM 121/122 (5+5), or PHYS 211/212 (4+4), each with lab/recitation; encoded at 4 credits with the CHEM 5-credit alternative documented in the choice notes. COSC electives: catalog requires 17 credits of COSC 200-400 (19 if COSC 161 is taken instead of COSC 160/160L); the sample shows six 3-credit elective slots (18 credits). COSC 161 (Java Essentials for Experienced Programmers, 1 cr) may substitute for COSC 160/160L for students with prior programming experience — alternate path noted, not separately encoded. COSC 142 (Professional Development) is waived if the student completed a professional development course through another School of Science and Engineering major. Grade of C or better required in all COSC courses; each COSC course may be repeated at most once (a withdrawal does not count). MATH 105 / COSC 145 are advisory placement-prep courses only, not degree requirements, and are excluded from the plan (they count toward the 120 if taken). Bridges core courses (Writing and Analysis, Essential Questions Seminar, etc.) are listed by name only on the official sample sequence with no published course codes, so they are encoded as choice slots with placeholder codes; no codes invented. Prereqs intentionally left empty: the official sample sequence states an ordering but publishes no prerequisite list. Sources: https://www.duq.edu/academics/colleges-and-schools/science-and-engineering/academics/departments-and-programs/mathematics-and-computer-science/undergraduate-programs/ba-bs-computer-science.php and https://www.duq.edu/academics/university-catalogs/2026-2027-catalog/undergraduate/academic-programs/science/math-and-computer-science.php
